A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
breast conservation therapy does not provide a better quality of life than mastectomy, but patients receiving mastectomy do have more problems with clothing and appearance.

women with early stage breast cancer who have a choice between breast conserving surgery and mastectomy have similar outcomes in terms of their quality of life, psychological adjustment, and performance status.
women with breast cancer are not adversely affected by their surgical treatment and are able to maintain their quality of life and psychological adjustment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of breast conservation therapy or mastectomy is a very personal one.
women with early breast cancer should not be denied a breast‐conserving approach because of fears that their quality of life will be adversely affected.
